description.narrative: The most significant expected project-level outcome is an improvement in access to quality medical products and equipment in Egypt and East African countries, notably in Kenya, Ethiopia, Tanzania, Rwanda and Uganda. Beyond the project, IFC anticipates that its financing will contribute to increasing the competitive pressures of the Egyptian and East African medical equipment distribution market, by supporting the Companys business-as-usual operational model of integrating high value-added services with medical device distribution, and internationalization through sole distributorship and principal diversification.

The proposed investment is a USD15M unsecured income participating loan, in GMED Holding B.V. (the Company under creation, the Borrower) a holding medical technologies (medtech) manufacturing and distribution company, to support (i) growing its existing subsidiaries' operations in Egypt and (ii) the company's expansion plan in tofive East African countries as a medtech distributor (the Project).
